identity.name: Sodium/potassium/calcium salts of fatty acids
synonyms: Salts of myristic, palmitic and stearic acids (calcium, potassium, sodium)
identity.chemical_class: Alkali/alkaline-earth metal salts of long-chain fatty acids (fatty-acid salts)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic fatty-acid salts reduce interfacial tension and improve powder flow/lubrication, supporting emulsification and anticaking under GMP use levels.

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for E470a/E470b.

efsa.key_finding: E470a/E470b were considered of no safety concern at reported uses/use levels; fatty-acid moiety contribution to saturated fat intake was estimated up to about 5%.

adi.basis: JECFA database entry for salts of myristic/palmitic/stearic acids (Ca/K/Na) lists ADI NOT SPECIFIED; WHO FAS monograph states ADI Not limited.

concerns.summary: Direct additive-specific subchronic/chronic/reproductive/developmental datasets for E470a salts are limited; EFSA relied partly on read-across and available supporting studies.
EFSA noted microbiota effects reported for some other emulsifiers, but no additive-specific microbiome studies were available for E470a/E470b.

A 2023 EFSA NDA assessment of mustard-derived behenic acid used to manufacture emulsifiers including E470a estimated reaction risk in mustard-allergic individuals as extremely unlikely (<=1%) under proposed conditions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018: no need for numerical ADI; no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.
JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED / Not limited for salts of myristic, palmitic and stearic acids (Ca/K/Na).
FDA eCFR: permitted salts-of-fatty-acids use under 21 CFR 172.863; calcium stearate affirmed GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1229.

adi_exceedance.notes: No current numerical ADI was set by EFSA/JECFA for this additive group; EFSA estimated E470a/E470b fatty-acid moieties contributed up to about 5% of overall saturated fatty-acid intake at mean exposure.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus (EFSA/JECFA/FDA) supports low concern at permitted use levels, but additive-specific long-term toxicology data are limited and some source-specific allergen context remains relevant.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 no-safety-concern conclusion with no numerical ADI needed
JECFA ADI NOT SPECIFIED / Not limited for corresponding salt group
FDA allowance under 21 CFR 172.863 and calcium stearate GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1229
No IARC classification entry for sodium/potassium/calcium stearate in current IARC dataset
Evidence gaps in dedicated additive-specific chronic/reproductive datasets
